A short distance later MY FLYING ANGEL then shifted out to improve, resulting in RICH HORSE shifting out and COUNTRY DANCER then having to be checked and blundering when it made contact with CHILL MASTER.  The Stewards were satisfied that there was not sufficient room for Jockey D B McMonagle to improve at that point and advised him in similar circumstances he should ensure that he exercises more care. He said TAIHANG SCENERY then continued to race ungenerously for some distance thereafter before giving ground in the Home Straight.  He added, in his opinion, TAIHANG SCENERY would be better suited over 1000 Metres.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea.  The performance of TAIHANG SCENERY was considered disappointing as compared to its previous race starts.  Before being allowed to race again, TAIHANG SCENERY will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination. horses.incident_text: When questioned E C W Wong stated that the instructions were to lead the event but if the pace was too strong he was given the option of taking a position with cover.  He said after SKY HEART commenced well and was positioned to the outside of SOLEIL FIGHTER he elected to take a position with cover and allow SWORD POINT and AWESOME FLUKE to cross his mount in the early stages.  He added as a consequence SKY HEART settled further back in the field than intended.  He said from the 700 Metres he placed SKY HEART under pressure, however, the horse lay in from that point, particularly in the Home Straight, and proved difficult to ride out.  He said he was further placed in some difficulty as he was riding the horse on a long rein which did not provide him with the necessary leverage to properly straighten the horse in the Home Straight.  Trainer C Fownes confirmed that the instructions were to lead and indicated that, in his view, Jockey Wong had made the decision to ride the horse with cover too prematurely.  After considering the evidence the matter was adjourned to a date to be fixed.  Sent for sampling post-race. <26/2/2026 Additional Veterinary Reports>The Veterinary Surgeon reported that SKY HEART was lame in its right front leg on the morning after racing. Before being allowed to race again, SKY HEART will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.<1/3/2026 Adjourned Inquiry> The Stewards today concluded an inquiry opened into Jockey E C W Wong’s riding of SKY HEART. Further evidence today was taken from Jockey Wong and Trainer C Fownes. The Stewards also considered a betting and analytical report provided by the Racing Integrity and Betting Analysis Department. That report did not identify any integrity concern in relation to the betting on the event. In addition, the Stewards considered a report from the Department of Veterinary Regulation, Welfare and Biosecurity Policy which confirmed SKY HEART had been found to be lame in the right front leg the day after racing. To verify the lameness, a Sleip analysis report was provided to the Stewards. After considering the evidence the Stewards advised Jockey Wong that, in their opinion, he had made two errors of judgement in the early stages. Firstly, not riding his mount with more intent in the early stages to attempt to cross SOLEIL FIGHTER as he had been instructed to do. Secondly, when positioned to the outside of SOLEIL FIGHTER in the early stages he elected to restrain his mount to race behind SOLEIL FIGHTER which resulted in SWORD POINT and AWESOME FLUKE being able to cross SKY HEART and SKY HEART then racing further back in the field. Having found that Jockey Wong had made those errors of judgement, the Stewards did not elect to issue a charge against Jockey Wong under Rule 99 (2) on the basis that they could not be satisfied, having regard to the horse being found to be lame after the race, that his actions had resulted in it not winning or obtaining the best possible place in the field. However, Jockey Wong was advised that his riding in the early stages lacked the necessary judgement of a jockey riding in this jurisdiction and he would be expected to make a greater effort in similar circumstance to comply with instructions he has been issued.
Jumped awkwardly.  Over the concluding stages had difficulty obtaining clear running when improving into a tight run between SOLEIL FIGHTER and HUGE WAVE.

When questioned B Avdulla stated that from the outside barrier he was instructed to hold a handy position if possible.  He said CALIFORNIATOTALITY jumped only fairly and when SOLEIL FIGHTER and SKY HEART showed good speed in the early stages and he was positioned to the outside of AWESOME FLUKE and SWORD POINT, which he had expected would go forward, he elected to shift CALIFORNIATOTALITY behind runners in the early stages to avoid covering additional ground.  He added his tactics were also influenced by the fact that CALIFORNIATOTALITY was racing first up from a break and was carrying top weight of 135 lbs.  Trainer A S Cruz confirmed the instructions issued and expressed satisfaction with Jockey Avdulla’s decision to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages, particularly having regard to the way it commenced the race and the fact that it was carrying top weight in the event.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Jockey Wong stated that from the outside barrier he had to ride his mount along in the early stages to go forward.  He said when unable to cross runners in the early stages he made the first turn wide.  He added that after obtaining a position outside KA YING WARRIOR in the Back Straight his mount failed to respond to his riding in the Home Straight. He said as a result for some distance in the middle stages he was obliged to restrain his mount to avoid SILVER SPURS.  He added due to the manner in which the horse raced during the early and middle stages it was left without a finishing effort in the Home Straight.  He further stated that when placed under pressure in the Home Straight his mount blundered leaving the 200 Metres and as a result he did not fully test it over the concluding stages when not in a competitive position.  Trainer D A Hayes advised that the horse had pleased him leading into tonight’s race but having regard to the performance he would now give the horse a freshen-up before its next race start.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of BUSTLING CITY was considered disappointing.
